class _ListStream:
    def __init__(self, sink):
        self.sink = sink

    def write(self, text):
        self.sink.append(text.rstrip("\n"))


def selftest(verbose=False):
    scratch = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="csm-selftest-", dir=os.environ.get("TMPDIR") or None)
    suite = Selftest(verbose=verbose)
    try:
        _unit_cases(suite)
        _e2e_cases(suite, scratch)
        _waiver_cases(suite, scratch)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
    total = suite.passed + suite.failed
    print("SELFTEST: passed=%d/%d failed=%d" % (suite.passed, total, suite.failed))
    return 0 if suite.failed == 0 else 1


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog=TOOL,
        description="Scan tracked files for session material.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--repo", help="git repository to read")
    parser.add_argument("--rev", default="HEAD", help="revision to scan (default HEAD)")
    parser.add_argument("--home-limit", type=int, default=DEFAULT_HOME_LIMIT,
                        help="distinct bare /home paths that make a listing (default %d)"
                             % DEFAULT_HOME_LIMIT)
    parser.add_argument("--scope", choices=("ufo", "all"), default=DEFAULT_SCOPE,
                        help="tracked paths to scan: all (default) or .ufo/ only")
    parser.add_argument("--account", default=None,
                        help="account name for R8 (default: the invoking account); "
                             "the value is never printed")
    parser.add_argument("--serial-from-host", action="store_true",
                        help="read the live monitor serial(s) with %s and count them "
                             "as plain substrings (R6); values are never printed"
                             % (HOST_CMD[0],))
    parser.add_argument("--waivers", default=DEFAULT_WAIVERS,
                        help="waiver registry, relative to the repo (default %s)" % DEFAULT_WAIVERS)
    parser.add_argument("--gate-source", default=DEFAULT_GATE_SOURCE,
                        help="gate source for kind=gate-copy (default %s)" % DEFAULT_GATE_SOURCE)
    parser.add_argument("--no-waivers", action="store_true",
                        help="ignore every synthetic-material marker")
    parser.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true", help="run positive/negative fixtures")
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="print passing selftest cases too")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.selftest:
        return selftest(verbose=args.verbose)
    if not args.repo:
        parser.error("--repo is required (or use --selftest)")
    if args.home_limit < 0:
        parser.error("--home-limit must be >= 0")
    if args.account is not None and not args.account.strip():
        parser.error("--account must not be empty")

    account = args.account if args.account is not None else invoking_account()
    if not account:
        sys.stderr.write("%s: note: no account resolved, R8 is inert "
                         "(pass --account)\n" % TOOL)

    try:
        serials = host_serials() if args.serial_from_host else ()
        sha, files, findings, waived, rejected = run(
            args.repo, args.rev, home_limit=args.home_limit,
            waivers=args.waivers, gate_source=args.gate_source,
            use_waivers=not args.no_waivers, scope=args.scope, serials=serials,
            account=account,
        )
    except GateError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("%s: error: %s\n" % (TOOL, exc))
        return 2
    return emit(sha, files, findings, waived, rejected)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-wave-done.py -- did every wave of a round reach WAVE-DONE?

Question answered: for round ``N`` at a revision, is there a committed
``<wave>-results.json`` for every committed ``.ufo/waves/round-N/<wave>.ready``,
and does every seat in it carry a terminal status? This is the mechanical form
of round-49 defect D2: the round-49 report was filed with 7 w1 seats unsettled
and no WAVE-DONE, and the closure could only read that out of prose.

Input: a git repository and a revision. Every file is read from the object
database (``git ls-tree`` + ``git show <rev>:<path>``); the working tree is
never read, so the gate scores committed bytes at any revision of a clone
without checkout. The gate never writes to the repository and needs no scratch
space. ``--selftest`` is the only mode that writes, and it refuses a work dir
under ``/tmp``, ``/var/tmp`` or ``/dev/shm``, and inside a home directory: a
fixture is a git repository with commits, so under a home it would be home state
(round-48 M48-10), and a killed run would leave it there. The home rule reads
``$HOME`` (falling back to ``USERPROFILE`` on hosts that set no ``$HOME``) *and*
the passwd home for the uid, and an absent home is an error -- a rule that reads
only ``$HOME`` is switched off by unsetting it, and its own proof would disappear
with it. A caller-declared scratch root (``--scratch-root``, round-58 lesson
M57-1: some hosts have no writable scratch outside home) waives the home refusal
and nothing else. The shared-scratch refusal folds letter case (round 59: the
compare applies ``os.path.normcase``, because ``realpath`` cannot case-fold a
prefix that is not on disk). The selftest asserts its exact case count
(``SELFTEST_CHECKS``) for the same reason.

The results-file contract (derived, not invented)
-------------------------------------------------
Two sources, both checked:

* the fleet dispatcher that writes the file, ``scripts/hyaku/inline-dispatcher.py:289-296``
  (fleet root, not this lane): one record per seat with the keys ``name``,
  ``agent``, ``output`` and ``note``, where ``note`` is ``None`` when the output
  was retained and the kernel-restart note when it was not; the document is
  ``{"lane", "round", "wave", "seats", "results"}``, and ``finalize`` writes it
  only when every seat has settled, beside the dispatch file;
* the round prompt's run-7 handoff block (``.ufo/prompts/mado-round-<N>.md``,
  "Inline spawn handoff"): "per seat: name, agent, id, status, final output".

Those two disagree: the prompt names an ``id`` and a ``status`` field, and the
dispatcher writes neither. Every ``*-results.json`` committed in this lane's
history (rounds 39-48, plus ``round-48/a4r1``) carries exactly the dispatcher's
four keys and no ``status``: a record there is terminal because the file only
exists after ``finalize``, not because a field says so. The gate therefore
scores *observable* terminal states, and accepts an explicit ``status`` string
if a future dispatcher writes one -- unknown values fail rather than pass, so
that drift becomes a finding instead of a silent OK.

Per-seat state, in this order (``name``/``agent`` first: a record without them
is not a seat record):

===========================  =============================================  ============
condition                    state                                           terminal
===========================  =============================================  ============
``name`` missing/empty       ``name-missing``                                no
``name`` not a plain id      ``name-malformed``                              no
``agent`` missing/empty      ``agent-missing``                               no
``name`` already seen        ``name-duplicate``                              no
``status`` = ``settled``     ``settled``                                     yes
``status`` = ``output-unavailable``  ``settled`` (lossy)                     yes
``status`` dead value        ``seat-dead`` (``failed``, ``error``,           yes (dead)
                             ``dead``, ``killed``, ``cancelled``,
                             ``canceled``, ``timeout``)
``status`` other string      ``status-unknown`` (value printed)              no
no ``status``: non-empty     ``settled``                                     yes
   string ``output``
no ``status``: ``output``    ``settled`` (lossy)                             yes
   null + non-empty ``note``
no ``status``: ``output``    ``output-empty``                                no
   null/blank, no ``note``
no ``status``: ``output``    ``output-type``                                 no
   not a string/None
===========================  =============================================  ============

A *settled* seat is one the orchestrator took a final answer from, including the
lossy kernel-restart case (the record exists, the output was not retained); a
*dead* seat failed terminally. Both are terminal answers, and only settled ones
count towards ``settled=``.

Wave verdict (``OK`` only when every check holds)
-------------------------------------------------
* the ``.ready`` marker parses as JSON -- it is the launch marker the prompt
  defines (``ready-unparsable``; a malformed marker does not un-launch a wave);
* a results file exists at the revision (``results-missing``);
* it parses as a JSON object whose ``results`` is a list (``results-unparsable``,
  ``results-shape``) and the list is non-empty (``results-empty``);
* its ``lane`` is ``mado`` and its ``round``/``wave`` agree with the path and
  ``--round`` (``results-identity``; this is the mado gate, so another lane's
  results file in a mado wave dir is a finding, not a pass), and its ``seats``
  integer equals ``len(results)`` (``results-count``);
* every seat is settled (``seats-not-terminal``, one ``SEAT`` line each);
* when the wave's dispatch file is readable at the revision, the results seat
  set equals the dispatch ``taskCall.tasks`` name set (``dispatch-mismatch``);
  when no dispatch file is readable the wave line prints ``dispatched=-`` and
  the gate declares that limit -- seat coverage is then unconfirmed, and saying
  so is the honest answer (``dispatch-unparsable`` covers a dispatch file that
  is present but is not the expected shape).

A wave with no ``.ready`` file was never launched by this handoff, so it is not
scored. That is also the gate's scope: it scores the inline-spawn era, whose
launch marker is the committed ``.ready``. A round whose waves were launched by
the older dispatch bridge (rounds <= 38 in this lane) carries no ``.ready`` at
all, so it reads ``waves=0`` and a ``SCOPE`` line saying the round is *out of
scope*, not settled, so ``waves=0`` never reads as a clean round.

Output, one line per launched wave::

    WAVE wave=w1 ready=1 results=present seats=41 dispatched=41 settled=41 verdict=OK reason=none
    WAVE wave=w2 ready=1 results=absent seats=0 dispatched=- settled=0 verdict=MISSING reason=results-missing

one ``SEAT`` line per non-settled seat (seat names are not session material)::

    SEAT wave=w1 name=ExecFoo state=output-empty:null-no-note

one ``NOTE`` line per structural detail that has no place in the reason token,
one ``ORPHAN`` line per ``<wave>-results.json`` with no ``.ready`` beside it
(printed, never fatal: a stale results file is not a launched wave), one
``SCOPE`` line when the round has no launch marker at all::

    SCOPE round=42 markers=0 note=no-launch-marker: committed evidence without a .ready; ...
    SCOPE round=50 markers=0 note=round-absent: no committed evidence of this round at the revision

then the summary line, exactly::

    MADO_WAVE_DONE: round=49 waves=1 settled=0 verdict=MISSING

``waves=`` counts the launched waves (``.ready`` files) and ``settled=`` the
waves with verdict ``OK``. A round with no launched wave prints ``waves=0`` and
``verdict=MISSING``: "nothing was launched" is not "everything completed".

Exit status: 0 verdict OK, 1 verdict MISSING, 2 usage or git error (an
unresolvable ``--rev``, a ``--repo`` that is not a git repository, a bad
``--round``, a refused work dir).

Usage::

    check-wave-done.py --repo <dir> --rev <rev> --round N
    check-wave-done.py --selftest [--work <dir>] [--verbose]
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

WAVE_DIR = ".ufo/waves/round-%d"
READY_SUFFIX = ".ready"
RESULTS_SUFFIX = "-results.json"
DISPATCH_SUFFIX = "-dispatch.json"

# Recognised explicit `status` values, should a dispatcher ever write one.
SETTLED_STATUS = frozenset({"settled", "output-unavailable"})
DEAD_STATUS = frozenset({"failed", "error", "dead", "killed", "cancelled", "canceled",
                         "timeout"})

REFUSED_WORK_PREFIXES = ("/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/dev/shm")

# The exact number of assertions --selftest must make. A case that silently disappears (an
# env-dependent skip, a removed fixture) turns into a failure instead of a smaller green run.
# 62 portable cases; +1 on Windows for the case-variation pin (round-59 carry-in), which
# exists only where os.path.normcase folds -- on POSIX it is skipped by construction.
SELFTEST_CHECKS = 63 if os.name == "nt" else 62

NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$")
UNSAFE_DETAIL_RE = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+")

GIT_ENV_KEYS = ("PATH", "SYSTEMROOT")


class GateError(Exception):
    """A condition that makes the question unanswerable (exit 2)."""


def git_env(home=None):
    """Environment for read-only git calls: no user/system config, no locale drift."""
    env = {k: os.environ[k] for k in GIT_ENV_KEYS if k in os.environ}
    env.setdefault("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin")
    env["HOME"] = home or os.environ.get("HOME") or "/nonexistent"
    env["GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM"] = "1"
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS"] = "0"
    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
    return env


def run_git(repo, args):
    cmd = ["git", "-C", repo] + list(args)
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, env=git_env())
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise GateError("%s exited %d: %s" % (" ".join(cmd), proc.returncode,
                                              proc.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()))
    return proc.stdout


def resolve_rev(repo, rev):
    if not rev or not rev.strip():
        raise GateError("--rev is empty")
    out = run_git(repo, ["rev-parse", "--verify", "--end-of-options", rev + "^{commit}"])
    sha = out.decode().strip()
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?", sha):
        raise GateError("--rev %r did not resolve to one commit (%r)" % (rev, sha))
    return sha


def check_repo(repo):
    if not os.path.isdir(repo):
        raise GateError("--repo %r is not a directory" % repo)
    run_git(repo, ["rev-parse", "--git-dir"])


def read_blob(repo, sha, path):
    """Committed bytes of `path` at commit `sha`; GateError when absent."""
    return run_git(repo, ["show", "%s:%s" % (sha, path)])


def try_read_blob(repo, sha, path):
    try:
        return read_blob(repo, sha, path)
    except GateError:
        return None


def blobs_at(repo, sha, path):
    """Every blob path at `sha` under `path` (files only), repo-relative."""
    if not path.endswith("/"):
        path += "/"
    out = run_git(repo, ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--name-only", "--full-tree", sha, "--", path])
    return [p for p in out.decode("utf-8", "replace").split("\0") if p]


def sanitize(text):
    return UNSAFE_DETAIL_RE.sub("_", str(text)).strip("_")[:60] or "none"


def seat_state(rec):
    """(state, detail) for one results record; state 'settled' means settled."""
    if not isinstance(rec, dict):
        return "record-type", type(rec).__name__
    name = rec.get("name")
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
        return "name-missing", None
    if not NAME_RE.match(name.strip()):
        return "name-malformed", None
    agent = rec.get("agent")
    if not isinstance(agent, str) or not agent.strip():
        return "agent-missing", name.strip()
    if "status" in rec and rec["status"] is not None:
        st = rec["status"]
        if not isinstance(st, str):
            return "status-unknown", type(st).__name__
        key = st.strip().lower()
        if key in SETTLED_STATUS:
            return "settled", key
        if key in DEAD_STATUS:
            return "seat-dead", key
        return "status-unknown", key
    out = rec.get("output")
    if out is None:
        note = rec.get("note")
        if isinstance(note, str) and note.strip():
            return "settled", "lossy"
        return "output-empty", "null-no-note"
    if isinstance(out, str):
        if out.strip():
            return "settled", "output"
        return "output-empty", "blank-output"
    return "output-type", type(out).__name__


def parse_results(blob, wave, rnd):
    """(records, reasons, detail) for a results blob; records None on a shape failure."""
    try:
        doc = json.loads(blob.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    except ValueError as exc:
        return None, ["results-unparsable"], sanitize(exc)
    if not isinstance(doc, dict):
        return None, ["results-shape"], type(doc).__name__
    recs = doc.get("results")
    if not isinstance(recs, list):
        return None, ["results-shape"], type(recs).__name__
    reasons = []
    if doc.get("wave") != wave:
        reasons.append("results-identity")
    if doc.get("round") != rnd:
        reasons.append("results-identity")
    if doc.get("lane") != "mado":
        reasons.append("results-identity")
    seats = doc.get("seats")
    if not isinstance(seats, int) or isinstance(seats, bool) or seats != len(recs):
        reasons.append("results-count")
    return recs, reasons, None


def dispatch_head(repo, sha, wave, round_dir, ready_doc):
    """(names, source) from the wave's dispatch file at `sha`; names None when unreadable."""
    candidates = [round_dir + "/" + wave + DISPATCH_SUFFIX]
    ref = (ready_doc or {}).get("dispatch") if isinstance(ready_doc, dict) else None
    if isinstance(ref, str) and ref:
        if os.path.isabs(ref):
            # A scratch dispatch path is not in the object database; only its
            # basename can name the committed copy beside the ready marker.
            candidates.append(round_dir + "/" + os.path.basename(ref))
        else:
            candidates.append(ref.lstrip("/"))
            candidates.append(round_dir + "/" + os.path.basename(ref))
    for cand in dict.fromkeys(candidates):
        blob = try_read_blob(repo, sha, cand)
        if blob is None:
            continue
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(blob.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        except ValueError:
            return None, cand
        tasks = ((parsed or {}).get("taskCall") or {}).get("tasks")
        if not isinstance(tasks, list):
            return None, cand
        names = []
        for task in tasks:
            if not isinstance(task, dict) or not isinstance(task.get("name"), str):
                return None, cand
            names.append(task["name"])
        return names, cand
    return None, None


def check_wave(repo, sha, rnd, round_dir, blob_path):
    """(wave line, seat lines, note lines, settled?) for one launched wave."""
    wave = os.path.basename(blob_path)[:-len(READY_SUFFIX)]
    reasons = []
    notes = []
    seat_lines = []

    ready_blob = try_read_blob(repo, sha, blob_path)
    ready_doc = None
    if ready_blob is not None:
        try:
            ready_doc = json.loads(ready_blob.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        except ValueError:
            ready_doc = None
    if not isinstance(ready_doc, dict):
        reasons.append("ready-unparsable")

    res_blob = try_read_blob(repo, sha, round_dir + "/" + wave + RESULTS_SUFFIX)
    seats = 0
    settled = 0
    seat_names = []

    if res_blob is None:
        reasons.append("results-missing")
        recs = None
    else:
        recs, hard, detail = parse_results(res_blob, wave, rnd)
        reasons.extend(hard)
        if detail:
            notes.append("NOTE wave=%s reason=results-unparsable detail=%s" % (wave, detail))
        if recs is None:
            recs = None
        else:
            seats = len(recs)
            if not recs:
                reasons.append("results-empty")
            seen = set()
            for rec in recs:
                state, detail = seat_state(rec)
                name = rec.get("name") if isinstance(rec, dict) else None
                if isinstance(name, str) and name.strip():
                    key = name.strip()
                    if key in seen and state == "settled":
                        state, detail = "name-duplicate", key
                    seen.add(key)
                if state == "settled":
                    settled += 1
                    seat_names.append(name.strip() if isinstance(name, str) else "")
                else:
                    tag = state if not detail else "%s:%s" % (state, detail)
                    seat_lines.append("SEAT wave=%s name=%s state=%s"
                                      % (wave, name if isinstance(name, str) else "-", tag))
            if settled != seats:
                reasons.append("seats-not-terminal")

    names_d, src = dispatch_head(repo, sha, wave, round_dir, ready_doc)
    dispatched = "-"
    if src is not None and names_d is None:
        reasons.append("dispatch-unparsable")
        dispatched = "unparsable"
    if names_d is not None:
        dispatched = str(len(names_d))
        if recs is not None:
            missing = [n for n in names_d if n not in seat_names]
            extra = [n for n in seat_names if n not in names_d]
            if missing or extra:
                reasons.append("dispatch-mismatch")
                seat_lines.append("SEAT wave=%s state=dispatch-mismatch missing=%d extra=%d"
                                  % (wave, len(missing), len(extra)))

    reasons = list(dict.fromkeys(reasons))
    ok = not reasons
    line = ("WAVE wave=%s ready=1 results=%s seats=%d dispatched=%s settled=%d verdict=%s reason=%s"
            % (wave, "present" if res_blob is not None else "absent", seats, dispatched,
               settled, "OK" if ok else "MISSING", "none" if ok else "+".join(reasons)))
    return line, seat_lines, notes, ok


def scan(repo, sha, rnd):
    """(wave lines, seat lines, notes, orphan lines, waves, settled) for one round."""
    round_dir = WAVE_DIR % rnd
    depth = round_dir.count("/") + 1
    paths = blobs_at(repo, sha, round_dir)
    ready = sorted(p for p in paths
                   if p.count("/") == depth and p.endswith(READY_SUFFIX))
    results = sorted(p for p in paths
                     if p.count("/") == depth and p.endswith(RESULTS_SUFFIX))

    wave_lines, seat_lines, note_lines = [], [], []
    waves = settled = 0
    for path in ready:
        line, seats, notes, ok = check_wave(repo, sha, rnd, round_dir, path)
        wave_lines.append(line)
        seat_lines.extend(seats)
        note_lines.extend(notes)
        waves += 1
        settled += 1 if ok else 0

    launched = {os.path.basename(p)[:-len(READY_SUFFIX)] for p in ready}
    orphan_lines = ["ORPHAN results=%s reason=no-ready" % os.path.basename(p)
                    for p in results
                    if os.path.basename(p)[:-len(RESULTS_SUFFIX)] not in launched]
    if not ready:
        # No launch marker: either the round left no committed evidence at all, or
        # its waves were launched by a path this gate does not score (the pre-handoff
        # dispatch bridge, rounds <= 38 in this lane). Say which; never let waves=0
        # read as a clean round.
        if paths:
            scope_lines = ["SCOPE round=%d markers=0 note=no-launch-marker: "
                           "committed evidence without a .ready; this gate scores the "
                           "inline-spawn handoff only, so the round is out of scope, "
                           "not settled" % rnd]
        else:
            scope_lines = ["SCOPE round=%d markers=0 note=round-absent: no committed "
                           "evidence of this round at the revision" % rnd]
    else:
        scope_lines = []
    return wave_lines, seat_lines, note_lines, orphan_lines, scope_lines, waves, settled


def run_check(args):
    check_repo(args.repo)
    if args.round < 0:
        raise GateError("--round must be >= 0 (got %d)" % args.round)
    sha = resolve_rev(args.repo, args.rev)
    (wave_lines, seat_lines, note_lines, orphan_lines, scope_lines,
     waves, settled) = scan(args.repo, sha, args.round)
    for line in wave_lines + seat_lines + note_lines + orphan_lines + scope_lines:
        print(line)
    verdict = "OK" if (waves > 0 and settled == waves) else "MISSING"
    print("MADO_WAVE_DONE: round=%d waves=%d settled=%d verdict=%s"
          % (args.round, waves, settled, verdict))
    return 0 if verdict == "OK" else 1

# selftest
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Suite:
    def __init__(self, verbose=False):
        self.verbose = verbose
        self.passed = 0
        self.failed = []

    def check(self, name, ok, detail=""):
        if ok:
            self.passed += 1
            if self.verbose:
                print("ok   %s %s" % (name, detail))
        else:
            self.failed.append((name, detail))
            print("FAIL %s %s" % (name, detail))

    def report(self):
        total = self.passed + len(self.failed)
        if total != SELFTEST_CHECKS:
            self.failed.append(("selftest-count",
                                "expected=%d got=%d" % (SELFTEST_CHECKS, total)))
            total = self.passed + len(self.failed)
        for name, detail in self.failed:
            print("FAILED: %s %s" % (name, detail))
        print("MADO_WAVE_DONE_SELFTEST: %d/%d passed" % (self.passed, total))
        return 0 if not self.failed else 1


def passwd_home():
    """The passwd home for the current uid, or None when the platform has no passwd db."""
    try:
        import pwd
    except ImportError:
        return None
    try:
        return pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir
    except (KeyError, OSError):
        return None


def home_roots():
    """Every home this process could write under: $HOME (required, non-empty) and the passwd home.

    A rule that reads only $HOME is skippable by unsetting the variable, and the gate's own
    home-refusal cases would then vanish with it and still report success. So an absent or
    empty $HOME is an error, not "no home to compare", and the passwd home is checked too.
    """
    env_home = os.environ.get("HOME") or os.environ.get("USERPROFILE")
    if not env_home or not env_home.strip():
        raise GateError("HOME is unset or empty: the home rule cannot be checked, and an absent "
                        "HOME must not switch it off (set HOME and point --work at a scratch "
                        "filesystem)")
    roots = []
    for cand in (env_home, passwd_home()):
        if not cand:
            continue
        real = os.path.realpath(cand)
        if real != os.sep and real not in roots:
            roots.append(real)
    return roots


def resolve_work(explicit, declared_tree=None):
    # declared_tree (round-58, lesson M57-1): a caller-declared scratch tree. It may supply
    # the work root when --work is absent, and everything inside it is scratch by
    # declaration, so the home refusal never fires there. The shared-scratch prefixes are
    # refused in every mode. Fixtures are still git repositories with commits and files:
    # under a home they are home state (round-48 M48-10) the moment the caller declares
    # the location scratch instead.
    cand = explicit or declared_tree or os.environ.get("TMPDIR")
    if not cand:
        raise GateError("--selftest needs --work <dir> (or --scratch-root <dir>, or a TMPDIR) "
                        "outside /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm and the home directory")
    real = os.path.realpath(cand)
    folded = os.path.normcase(real)
    for bad in REFUSED_WORK_PREFIXES:
        # Compare the resolved prefix too: on Windows the literal POSIX prefix can never
        # match a drive-letter candidate, and "C:\\tmp" would slip past the rule. The
        # compare also folds letter case (os.path.normcase; identity on POSIX): realpath
        # cannot case-fold a prefix that is not on disk, so before round 59 a case-variant
        # spelling of an absent shared-scratch prefix (C:\\DEV\\shm for /dev/shm) matched
        # nothing and was accepted -- the r58 closure's C:/TMP residual, bypass receipt
        # .ufo/waves/round-59/receipts/casefold-before.txt, pin assertion
        # refuse-work-casefold below.
        real_bad = os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(bad))
        folded_bad = os.path.normcase(bad)
        if (folded == folded_bad or folded.startswith(folded_bad + os.sep)
                or folded == real_bad or folded.startswith(real_bad + os.sep)):
            raise GateError("refusing work dir under %s (got %s): use a scratch filesystem"
                            % (bad, real))
    inside_tree = False
    if declared_tree:
        tree_real = os.path.realpath(declared_tree)
        inside_tree = real == tree_real or real.startswith(tree_real + os.sep)
    if not inside_tree:
        for home in home_roots():
            if real == home or real.startswith(home + os.sep):
                raise GateError("refusing work dir inside the home directory (got ~%s): use a "
                                "scratch filesystem" % real[len(home):])
    os.makedirs(real, exist_ok=True)
    return tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="wave-done-selftest.", dir=real)


class Fixture:
    """A throwaway git repository holding wave markers, dispatch files and results."""

    def __init__(self, root, name):
        self.root = root
        self.path = os.path.join(root, name)
        os.makedirs(self.path, exist_ok=False)
        self.home = os.path.join(root, "home-" + name)
        for sub in ("", ".cache", ".config", ".local/share", ".local/state"):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(self.home, sub), exist_ok=True)
        self.env = git_env(self.home)
        self.env.update({"TMPDIR": self.root,
                         "XDG_CACHE_HOME": os.path.join(self.home, ".cache"),
                         "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": os.path.join(self.home, ".config"),
                         "XDG_DATA_HOME": os.path.join(self.home, ".local", "share"),
                         "XDG_STATE_HOME": os.path.join(self.home, ".local", "state")})
        self.git(["init", "-q"])
        top = self.git(["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"]).decode().strip()
        if os.path.realpath(top) != os.path.realpath(self.path):
            raise GateError("fixture toplevel %r != %r" % (top, self.path))

    def git(self, args):
        cmd = ["git", "-C", self.path,
               "-c", "user.name=Wave Done Selftest",
               "-c", "user.email=selftest@example.invalid",
               "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false",
               "-c", "tag.gpgsign=false"] + list(args)
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, env=self.env)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise GateError("fixture git %s: %s" % (" ".join(args),
                                                    proc.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()))
        return proc.stdout

    def write(self, rel, content):
        full = os.path.join(self.path, rel)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(full), exist_ok=True)
        data = content if isinstance(content, bytes) else content.encode()
        with open(full, "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(data)

    def commit(self, files, msg):
        for rel, content in sorted(files.items()):
            self.write(rel, content)
            self.git(["add", "--", rel])
        self.git(["commit", "-q", "-m", msg])
        return self.git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"]).decode().strip()


def results_doc(round_no, wave, records, seats=None, lane="mado"):
    return json.dumps({"lane": lane, "round": round_no, "wave": wave,
                       "seats": len(records) if seats is None else seats,
                       "results": records}, indent=1)


def dispatch_doc(names):
    return json.dumps({"taskCall": {"tasks": [{"name": n, "agent": "executor", "task": "x"}
                                              for n in names]}})


def seat(name, agent="executor", output="final answer", note=None, **extra):
    rec = {"name": name, "agent": agent, "output": output, "note": note}
    rec.update(extra)
    return rec


def invoke(repo, rev, rnd, work):
    """Run this file in check mode as a child process; (rc, stdout+stderr)."""
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-I", os.path.abspath(__file__),
           "--repo", repo, "--rev", rev, "--round", str(rnd)]
    env = git_env(os.path.join(work, "child-home"))
    os.makedirs(env["HOME"], exist_ok=True)
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, env=env, text=True)
    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout + proc.stderr


def summary_line(out):
    for line in reversed(out.strip().splitlines()):
        if line.startswith("MADO_WAVE_DONE:"):
            return line
    return ""


def first_line(out, prefix):
    for line in out.strip().splitlines():
        if line.startswith(prefix):
            return line
    return ""


def selftest(work, verbose=False):
    suite = Suite(verbose)
    rd = ".ufo/waves/round-49"
    lossy_note = ("orchestrator kernel restarted mid-wave; seat output was delivered to the "
                  "orchestrator session but not retained - read the seat report file")

    # A -- the round-49 shape: a launched wave and no results file (defect D2).
    a = Fixture(work, "r49-shape")
    sha = a.commit({rd + "/w1.ready": json.dumps({"lane": "mado", "round": 49, "wave": "w1",
                                                  "dispatch": "/scratch/x/w1-dispatch.json",
                                                  "l1": "MadoR49"}),
                    rd + "/w1-dispatch.json": dispatch_doc(["ExecA", "ExecB"])},
                   "round 49 wave 1 launched, no results")
    rc, out = invoke(a.path, sha, 49, work)
    suite.check("r49-exit-1", rc == 1, "rc=%d" % rc)
    suite.check("r49-summary",
                summary_line(out) == "MADO_WAVE_DONE: round=49 waves=1 settled=0 verdict=MISSING",
                summary_line(out))
    suite.check("r49-wave-line",
                first_line(out, "WAVE ") == ("WAVE wave=w1 ready=1 results=absent seats=0 "
                                             "dispatched=2 settled=0 verdict=MISSING "
                                             "reason=results-missing"),
                first_line(out, "WAVE "))
    suite.check("r49-no-seat-lines", first_line(out, "SEAT ") == "", first_line(out, "SEAT "))

    # B -- every seat settled.
    b = Fixture(work, "settled")

            variant_root = drive + os.sep + tail.lstrip("/\\").replace("/", os.sep).swapcase()
            cand = os.path.join(variant_root, "wave-done-selftest")
            plain = os.path.join(probe_real, "wave-done-selftest")
            folds = cand != plain and os.path.normcase(cand) == os.path.normcase(plain)
            chain = [cand, variant_root]
            existed = {p: os.path.exists(p) for p in chain}
            made = None
            try:
                made = resolve_work(cand)
                refused, detail = False, "accepted %s" % made
            except GateError as exc:
                refused, detail = True, str(exc)[:60]
            finally:
                if made is not None:
                    shutil.rmtree(made, ignore_errors=True)
                    for p in chain:
                        if not existed[p]:
                            shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True)
            suite.check("refuse-work-casefold", folds and refused,
                        "base=%s folds=%s %s" % (base, folds, detail))

    home = os.environ.get("HOME")

                            ("home-sub", os.path.join(home, "wave-done-selftest")),
                            ("passwd-home-sub",
                             os.path.join(passwd_home() or home, "wave-done-selftest"))):

            except GateError as exc:

            suite.check("refuse-work-%s" % label, refused, detail)

    # A rule that reads only $HOME is switched off by unsetting the variable, and its own two
    # cases above would vanish with it. Both directions are pinned: an absent HOME is an error
    # whatever the candidate, and the passwd home still refuses while HOME is absent.
    for label, cand in (("home-unset-pwdir", passwd_home() or work),
                        ("home-unset-safe-dir", work)):
        saved = os.environ.pop("HOME", None)
        try:
            try:
                resolve_work(cand)
                refused, detail = False, "accepted"
            except GateError as exc:
                refused, detail = True, str(exc)[:60]

            else:

        suite.check("refuse-work-%s" % label, refused, detail)

    # A caller-declared scratch tree (--scratch-root) waives the home refusal and nothing
    # else: the shared-scratch prefixes stay refused in every mode, so the waiver can
    # never be used to point the suite at /tmp-style scratch (round-58, lesson M57-1).
    existing_homes = [r for r in home_roots() if os.path.isdir(r)]
    if existing_homes:
        declared = os.path.join(existing_homes[0], "wave-done-selftest-declared")
        made = None
        try:
            made = resolve_work(declared, declared_tree=declared)
            suite.check("declared-root-accepts-home",
                        os.path.realpath(made).startswith(os.path.realpath(declared) + os.sep),
                        made)
        except (GateError, OSError) as exc:
            suite.check("declared-root-accepts-home", False, str(exc)[:60])
        finally:
            if made is not None:
                shutil.rmtree(made, ignore_errors=True)
            shutil.rmtree(declared, ignore_errors=True)
    else:
        suite.check("declared-root-accepts-home", False, "no existing home root")
    for bad_dir in ("/tmp/wave-done-selftest", "/var/tmp/wave-done-selftest",
                    "/dev/shm/wave-done-selftest"):
        try:
            resolve_work(bad_dir, declared_tree=work)
            refused, detail = False, "accepted"
        except GateError as exc:
            refused, detail = True, str(exc)[:60]
        suite.check("declared-root-refuse-%s" % bad_dir.strip("/").replace("/", "-"),
                    refused, detail)

    return suite.report()


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="check-wave-done.py",
        description="Score WAVE-DONE for every launched wave of a round, from committed bytes.")
    parser.add_argument("--repo", help="git repository (read-only)")
    parser.add_argument("--rev", help="revision whose committed bytes are scored")
    parser.add_argument("--round", type=int, help="round number: scans .ufo/waves/round-N")
    parser.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true", help="run the hermetic fixture suite")
    parser.add_argument("--work", help="scratch dir for --selftest (or TMPDIR); /tmp is refused")
    parser.add_argument("--scratch-root", metavar="DIR", dest="scratch_root",
                        help="caller-declared scratch root for --selftest: accepted even under "
                             "the home directory (shared-scratch prefixes stay refused)")
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="print every passing selftest case")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.selftest:
        if args.repo or args.rev or args.round is not None:
            parser.error("--selftest takes only --work/--scratch-root/--verbose")
        if args.work and args.scratch_root:
            parser.error("--work and --scratch-root are mutually exclusive")
        try:
            work = resolve_work(args.work, declared_tree=args.scratch_root)
        except GateError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("check-wave-done.py: %s\n" % exc)
            return 2
        try:
            return selftest(work, args.verbose)
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)

    if not args.repo or not args.rev or args.round is None:
        parser.error("--repo, --rev and --round are required (or use --selftest)")
    try:
        return run_check(args)
    except GateError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("check-wave-done.py: %s\n" % exc)
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""mado — calibration gate: the lane's published axis table must not be stale.

The lane publishes an axis table per round in prose inside SCORECARD.md
("Axis table re-derived at <state> ..."). AXES.md defines calibration as
"SHONEN.md/SCORECARD entries match observed repo state". This gate takes the
LAST such publication (history is never rewritten; the last line is the lane's
live publication) and re-derives each axis it can re-derive at the revision
under test, using that axis's own committed instrument.

Axes re-derived (frozen set):
  navigation   quality/check-index.py --rev <rev> --repo .   -> indexed=A/B
  calibration  .ufo/waves/round-31/c2/count.py <rev>         -> resolved_active=A active=B
  operability  quality/check-index.py --selftest             -> A/B assertions passed

A published fraction must equal the re-derived fraction. A missing publication, a
missing instrument or an unparsable cell is NOT a pass: it is counted as a
mismatch. Axes the gate cannot re-derive are not checked and are not claimed;
the gate prints which axes it checked.

Exit codes: 0 = every checked axis matches; 1 = at least one mismatch;
2 = usage or setup error.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

AXES = ("navigation", "calibration", "operability")
PUB_RE = re.compile(r"Axis table re-derived at")


def published_fractions(text):
    """Parse the last unquoted axis publication in a SCORECARD.md body.

    The publication is prose and may wrap across lines, so the body is flattened
    to one space-normalised string. The marker is the last "Axis table re-derived
    at" that is not immediately preceded by a quote or backtick (a later erratum
    that quotes the phrase must not replace the publication). The window is 2000
    characters, not 400, so a long publication is not silently truncated.
    """
    flat = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)
    marker = "Axis table re-derived at"
    idx = -1
    start = 0
    while True:
        found = flat.find(marker, start)
        if found < 0:
            break
        if found == 0 or flat[found - 1] not in "'\"`":
            idx = found
        start = found + len(marker)
    if idx < 0:
        return None, None
    line = flat[idx:idx + 2000]
    out = {}
    m = re.search(r"navigation (\d+)/(\d+)", line)
    if m:
        out["navigation"] = "%s/%s" % (m.group(1), m.group(2))
    m = re.search(r"calibration resolved-active (\d+)/(\d+)", line)
    if m:
        out["calibration"] = "%s/%s" % (m.group(1), m.group(2))
    m = re.search(r"operability selftest (\d+)/(\d+)", line)
    if m:
        out["operability"] = "%s/%s" % (m.group(1), m.group(2))
    return line, out


def compare(published, derived):
    """Pure comparison rule: published == derived, per checked axis.

    published: dict axis -> "a/b" (missing key = not published)
    derived:  dict axis -> "a/b" (missing key = not re-derivable)
    Returns (mismatches, rows) where rows is a list of (axis, published, derived, verdict).
    """
    rows, bad = [], 0
    for axis in AXES:
        pub = published.get(axis)
        der = derived.get(axis)
        if pub is None:
            verdict = "NOT-PUBLISHED"
        elif der is None:
            verdict = "NOT-RE-DERIVABLE"
        elif pub == der:
            verdict = "MATCH"
        else:
            verdict = "STALE"
        if verdict != "MATCH":
            bad += 1
        rows.append((axis, pub or "-", der or "-", verdict))
    return bad, rows


def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo] + list(args), capture_output=True, text=True,
                          env={k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("GIT_")})


def show(repo, rev, path):
    p = git(repo, "show", "%s:%s" % (rev, path))
    if p.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return p.stdout


def run_script(repo, rev, path, args, timeout=300):
    """Run a committed script's bytes at <rev> against the repo (read-only git)."""
    src = show(repo, rev, path)
    if src is None:
        return None, "instrument absent at %s: %s" % (rev, path)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="mado-axis-") as tmp:
        f = os.path.join(tmp, os.path.basename(path))
        with open(f, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(src)
        try:
            p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", f] + list(args), cwd=repo,
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout,
                               env={k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("GIT_")})
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, "instrument timed out: %s" % path
        return (p.stdout + p.stderr), None


def derive(repo, rev):
    derived, notes = {}, []

    out, err = run_script(repo, rev, "quality/check-index.py", ["--rev", rev, "--repo", "."])
    if err:
        notes.append(err)
    else:
        m = re.search(r"indexed=(\d+)/(\d+)", out or "")
        if m:
            derived["navigation"] = "%s/%s" % (m.group(1), m.group(2))
        else:
            notes.append("navigation: no indexed=A/B in check-index.py output")

    out, err = run_script(repo, rev, ".ufo/waves/round-31/c2/count.py", [rev])
    if err:
        notes.append(err)
    else:
        m = re.search(r"resolved_active=(\d+)", out or "")
        a = re.search(r"\bactive=(\d+)", out or "")
        if m and a:
            derived["calibration"] = "%s/%s" % (m.group(1), a.group(1))
        else:
            notes.append("calibration: no resolved_active/active in count.py output")

    out, err = run_script(repo, rev, "quality/check-index.py", ["--selftest"])
    if err:
        notes.append(err)
    else:
        m = re.search(r"(\d+)/(\d+) assertions passed", out or "")
        if m:
            derived["operability"] = "%s/%s" % (m.group(1), m.group(2))
        else:
            notes.append("operability: no A/B assertions passed in selftest output")

    return derived, notes


def selftest():
    fails = 0

    def check(name, cond):
        nonlocal fails
        if not cond:
            fails += 1
            print("FAIL %s" % name)
        else:
            print("PASS %s" % name)

    line, pub = published_fractions(
        "before the data commit `f621e3c0` (base `274f7355`, r30 tip). Axis table\n"
        "re-derived at base (criterion 22): navigation 43/43 = 1.0; calibration\n"
        "resolved-active 39/40 = 0.9750 (lowest — criterion 35's mis-scoped M23-7);\n"
        "sourced-art 1.0; operability selftest 9/9 = 1.0. Three claims, three\n"
        "distinct surfaces; each measured without the others.")
    check("parse-navigation", pub.get("navigation") == "43/43")
    check("parse-calibration", pub.get("calibration") == "39/40")
    check("parse-operability", pub.get("operability") == "9/9")
    check("ignore-sourced-art", "sourced-art" not in pub)

    bad, rows = compare(pub, {"navigation": "43/43", "calibration": "41/41",
                              "operability": "12/12"})
    check("stale-detected", bad == 2)
    check("stale-rows", [r[3] for r in rows] == ["MATCH", "STALE", "STALE"])

    bad, _ = compare(pub, {"navigation": "43/43", "calibration": "41/41",
                           "operability": "12/12"})
    check("nonzero-on-stale", bad != 0)

    bad, rows = compare({"navigation": "43/43", "calibration": "41/41",
                          "operability": "12/12"},
                         {"navigation": "43/43", "calibration": "41/41",
                          "operability": "12/12"})
    check("clean-is-zero", bad == 0)
    check("clean-rows", all(r[3] == "MATCH" for r in rows))

    bad, rows = compare({"navigation": "43/43"}, {"navigation": "43/43",
                                                   "calibration": "41/41",
                                                   "operability": "12/12"})
    check("missing-publication-is-not-a-pass", bad == 2)

    bad, rows = compare(pub, {"navigation": "43/43"})
    check("missing-instrument-is-not-a-pass", bad == 2)

    bad, rows = compare(pub, {"navigation": "43/43", "calibration": "41/41",
                              "operability": "12/12"})
    check("one-perturbation-bites", bad == 2)

    check("no-publication", published_fractions("nothing here")[0] is None)

    quoted = (
        "Axis table re-derived at tip: navigation 46/46 = 1.0; calibration "
        "resolved-active 41/41 = 1.0; operability selftest 12/12 = 1.0. "
        "Erratum: the older line 'Axis table re-derived at base: navigation "
        "43/43 = 1.0; calibration resolved-active 39/40 = 0.9750; operability "
        "selftest 9/9 = 1.0' is a quotation."
    )
    _, shadowed = published_fractions(quoted)
    check("quoted-marker-does-not-shadow", shadowed.get("calibration") == "41/41")
    check("quoted-marker-keeps-operability", shadowed.get("operability") == "12/12")

    long_pub = (
        "Axis table re-derived at tip: navigation 46/46 = 1.0; " + ("x" * 500)
        + " calibration resolved-active 41/41 = 1.0; operability selftest 12/12 = 1.0."
    )
    _, long_parsed = published_fractions(long_pub)
    check("long-publication-not-truncated", long_parsed.get("operability") == "12/12")

    bad, _ = compare(
        {"navigation": "40/46", "calibration": "41/41", "operability": "12/12"},
        {"navigation": "46/46", "calibration": "41/41", "operability": "12/12"},
    )
    check("navigation-perturbation-bites", bad == 1)
    bad, _ = compare(
        {"navigation": "46/46", "calibration": "41/41", "operability": "9/12"},
        {"navigation": "46/46", "calibration": "41/41", "operability": "12/12"},
    )
    check("operability-perturbation-bites", bad == 1)

    total = 18
    print("MADO_AXIS_SELFTEST: %d/%d assertions passed" % (total - fails, total))
    return 1 if fails else 0


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="calibration gate for the published axis table")
    ap.add_argument("--rev", help="revision to test (default: the repo's HEAD commit)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default=".", help="lane repo")
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.selftest:
        return selftest()

    repo = os.path.abspath(args.repo)
    if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(repo, ".git")):
        print("MADO_AXIS: SETUP_ERROR not a git repo: %s" % repo)
        return 2
    rev = args.rev
    if not rev:
        r = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
        if r.returncode != 0:
            print("MADO_AXIS: SETUP_ERROR cannot resolve HEAD")
            return 2
        rev = r.stdout.strip()
    v = git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--end-of-options", rev + "^{commit}")
    if v.returncode != 0:
        print("MADO_AXIS: SETUP_ERROR bad revision: %s" % rev)
        return 2
    rev = v.stdout.strip()

    body = show(repo, rev, "SCORECARD.md")
    if body is None:
        print("MADO_AXIS: SETUP_ERROR no SCORECARD.md at %s" % rev)
        return 2
    line, pub = published_fractions(body)
    derived, notes = derive(repo, rev)
    if pub is None:
        bad, rows = len(AXES), [(a, "-", derived.get(a, "-"), "NOT-PUBLISHED") for a in AXES]
    else:
        bad, rows = compare(pub, derived)

    for axis, p, d, verdict in rows:
        print("MADO_AXIS_ROW: axis=%s published=%s derived=%s verdict=%s" % (axis, p, d, verdict))
    for n in notes:
        print("MADO_AXIS_NOTE: %s" % n)
    print("MADO_AXIS: checked=%d mismatched=%d rev=%s" % (len(AXES), bad, rev))
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check QUALITY criterion 107 against immutable git objects at --rev."""
import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROW_START = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}\|")
ID_CELL = re.compile(r"S[0-9]{3,}")
REG_ROW = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}\|\s*(S[0-9]{3,})\s*\|")
FENCE = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}(```|~~~)")
URL = re.compile(r"https?://\S+")
PIN = re.compile(r"(?:^|\s)pin\s+([^\s]+)")
PIN_CELL = re.compile(r"([^:\s]+):([0-9]+)")
LOCATOR = re.compile(r"([0-9]+)(?:-([0-9]+))?")

class SetupError(Exception):
    pass

def git_blob(repo, rev, path, env):
    result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "cat-file", "blob", f"{rev}:{path}"],
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
    if result.returncode:
        raise SetupError(f"absent {rev}:{path}")
    return result.stdout

def cells(line):
    text = line.strip()
    if text.startswith("|"):
        text = text[1:]
    if text.endswith("|"):
        text = text[:-1]
    return [cell.strip() for cell in text.split("|")]

def visible_table_lines(text):
    in_fence = False
    in_comment = False
    for number, line in enumerate(text.split("\n"), 1):
        cursor = 0
        visible = ""
        while cursor < len(line):
            if in_comment:
                end = line.find("-->", cursor)
                if end < 0:
                    cursor = len(line)
                else:
                    cursor = end + 3
                    in_comment = False
            else:
                start = line.find("<!--", cursor)
                if start < 0:
                    visible += line[cursor:]
                    break
                visible += line[cursor:start]
                cursor = start + 4
                in_comment = True
        if not in_comment and FENCE.match(visible):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if not in_fence and not in_comment and ROW_START.match(visible):
            yield number, visible

def parse_registry(text):
    found = {}
    for raw in text.split("\n"):
        match = REG_ROW.match(raw)
        if match:
            row = cells(raw)
            found.setdefault(match.group(1), []).append(row)
    return found

def occurrences(anchor, name):
    # Prefix exclusion is identifier-only; slash and hyphen are valid boundaries.
    pattern = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(name) + r":")
    for match in pattern.finditer(anchor):
        rest = anchor[match.end():]
        first = LOCATOR.match(rest)
        if not first:
            continue
        locs = [(int(first.group(1)), int(first.group(2) or first.group(1)))]
        pos = first.end()
        while pos < len(rest):
            next_item = re.match(r", ?([0-9]+)(?:-([0-9]+))?", rest[pos:])
            if not next_item:
                break
            locs.append((int(next_item.group(1)), int(next_item.group(2) or next_item.group(1))))
            pos += next_item.end()
        rendered = ",".join(str(lo) if lo == hi else f"{lo}-{hi}" for lo, hi in locs)
        yield locs, rendered

def main(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--repo", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--rev", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--entry", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--registry", default="corpus/SOURCES.md")
    parser.add_argument("--work", required=True)
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
        os.makedirs(args.work, exist_ok=True)
        env = {"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"), "HOME": args.work,
               "TMPDIR": args.work, "LC_ALL": "C"}
        registry = parse_registry(git_blob(args.repo, args.rev, args.registry, env).decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        entry_bytes = git_blob(args.repo, args.rev, args.entry, env)
        entry = entry_bytes.decode("utf-8", "replace")
        pin_cache = {}
        out = []
        rows = 0
        covered = 0
        for line_no, raw in visible_table_lines(entry):
            row = cells(raw)
            if len(row) < 3 or not ID_CELL.fullmatch(row[2]):
                continue
            rows += 1
            row_id, sid = row[0] if row else "", row[2]
            pin_cell = row[3] if len(row) > 3 else ""
            pin_match = PIN_CELL.fullmatch(pin_cell)
            if pin_match is None:
                fallback = re.match(r"[^:\s]+:([0-9]+)", pin_cell)
                line = int(fallback.group(1)) if fallback else 0
                out.append(f"ANCHOR_COVER: row={row_id} sid={sid} line={line} name=- locators=none eof=unchecked verdict=MISS reason=malformed-pin")
                continue
            line = int(pin_match.group(2))
            records = registry.get(sid, [])
            if not records:
                out.append(f"ANCHOR_COVER: row={row_id} sid={sid} line={line} name=- locators=none eof=unchecked verdict=MISS reason=no-registry-row")
                continue
            if len(records) != 1:
                out.append(f"ANCHOR_COVER: row={row_id} sid={sid} line={line} name=- locators=none eof=unchecked verdict=MISS reason=dup-id")
                continue
            record = records[0]
            if len(record) < 6:
                raise SetupError(f"registry row {sid} has fewer than six cells")
            urls = URL.findall(record[1])
            name = urls[-1].rstrip(").,;").rsplit("/", 1)[-1] if urls else ""
            if not name or "#" in name or "?" in name:
                out.append(f"ANCHOR_COVER: row={row_id} sid={sid} line={line} name={name or '-'} locators=none eof=unchecked verdict=MISS reason=no-name")
                continue
            anchor = record[5]
            counted = list(occurrences(anchor, name))
            all_locs = [loc for locs, _ in counted for loc in locs]
            loc_text = ",".join(rendered for _, rendered in counted) if counted else "none"
            pin_match = PIN.search(anchor)
            eof = "unchecked"
            past_eof = False
            if pin_match:
                pin_path = pin_match.group(1).rstrip(".,;)")
                if pin_path not in pin_cache:
                    pin_cache[pin_path] = len(git_blob(args.repo, args.rev, pin_path, env).split(b"\n"))
                eof = "checked"
                past_eof = any(max(lo, hi) > pin_cache[pin_path] for lo, hi in all_locs)
            cover = any(lo <= hi and lo <= line <= hi for locs, _ in counted for lo, hi in locs)
            reason = "past-eof" if past_eof else ("no-cover" if not cover else "")
            ok = bool(cover and not past_eof)
            covered += int(ok)
            suffix = f" reason={reason}" if reason else ""
            out.append(f"ANCHOR_COVER: row={row_id} sid={sid} line={line} name={name} locators={loc_text} eof={eof} verdict={'OK' if ok else 'MISS'}{suffix}")
        for line in out:
            print(line)
        miss = rows - covered
        ok = rows > 0 and miss == 0
        print(f"CHECK107: rows={rows} covered={covered} miss={miss} verdict={'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
        return 0 if ok else 1
    except (SetupError, OSError, UnicodeError) as error:
        print(f"check107: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Round-27 successor of the QUALITY criterion 36 checker (round-26 spot-check §7 repairs 2 and 5).

Usage:
    python3 -I check-control-receipts.py --round N --data-registry PATH [--repo PATH] [--tip REV]
                                         [--shapes S1,S2,...] [--seeds N]
                                         [--receipt-glob PATTERN ...] [--any-md] [--counter-sha SHA]

Reads only git history and blobs at TIP (git log, show) with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0; never writes.

Rule (one sentence): exit 0 only if, at TIP, the oldest commit that adds a qualifying control
receipt under `.ufo/waves/round-N/controls/` has a committer time strictly earlier than the
`createdAt` of the named data-wave registry, and every named shape is covered by at least
`--seeds` distinct qualifying receipts; exit 1 otherwise; exit 2 when the history cannot be
evaluated.

Differences from the round-26 checker (which stays in round-26/quality/ and is read-only here):
  * `--receipt-glob PATTERN` (repeatable) — repair 5. Round-26's pre-data controls landed as
    `.txt` counter transcripts and the round-26 checker, which only ever looked at `.md`, exited
    1 with `reason=no-receipt-under-...`. A receipt is now selected by extension/path instead
    of format. Default patterns are `*.md` and `*.txt`; a pattern matches a controls/ path when
    it matches the path relative to `controls/` or that path's basename (case-insensitive and
    `*` crosses `/`), so the defaults reach every depth (`controls/v2/x.txt` included). A
    pattern that matches nothing is not an error: it fails as `receipts=0`.
  * The `CONTROL ` / `# Control` marker line is required of markdown receipts only. A verbatim
    counter log carries `exit=` and no markdown marker by construction; demanding one would
    keep repair 5 red. `--any-md` keeps its round-26 meaning (every markdown receipt under the
    globs qualifies, marker or not).
  * `--seeds N` (default 1) — repair 2, M26-9. Every named shape must be covered by at least N
    distinct receipts; a receipt covers a shape when its file name contains one of the shape's
    `|` alternatives (case-insensitive). A pre-data control set registered "two fresh seeds"
    per shape therefore fails at one receipt per shape instead of passing.
  * `--counter-sha SHA` (repeatable), the `updatedAt` exclusion and the strict `<` ordering are
    unchanged from round 26, as are the exit codes and the printed field order (new fields are
    appended, so a stored round-26 receipt line remains a substring of the current line).

Definitions
  qualifying receipt  a file under `.ufo/waves/round-N/controls/` (any depth) matching one of
                      `--receipt-glob`; a `.md` receipt additionally needs a line starting with
                      `CONTROL ` or `# Control` (case-sensitive) unless --any-md is given; and,
                      when `--counter-sha` is given, whose first line names one of those shas.
  receipt commit      the oldest commit reachable from TIP (`git log --reverse --diff-filter=A`)
                      adding a qualifying file; its committer time (`%ct`). Older wins: a later
                      receipt commit never supplies the timestamp.
  data registry       PATH (repo-relative), read at TIP; its JSON `createdAt` (ISO 8601) is when
                      the data seats were created. `updatedAt` is never consulted.
  shapes              comma list (default: DoNothing,EmptyArray|AllFalse,Junk,Echo,LabelKeyed,
                      NoReader); both coverage and seed counts key on the receipt file name,
                      after the glob and marker/sha filters.

Exit codes: 0 pass; 1 fail; 2 unevaluable (bad tip, unreadable registry, no adding commit).
"""
import argparse, datetime, fnmatch, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

DEFAULT_SHAPES = "DoNothing,EmptyArray|AllFalse,Junk,Echo,LabelKeyed,NoReader"
DEFAULT_GLOBS = ("*.md", "*.txt")
HEX64 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$")


def git(repo, *args):
    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS="0")
    for k in ("GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "GIT_INDEX_FILE"):
        env.pop(k, None)
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo] + list(args), capture_output=True, env=env)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout


def sha_arg(value):
    if not HEX64.match(value):
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("--counter-sha expects 64 hex characters, got %r" % value)
    return value.lower()


def seeds_arg(value):
    try:
        n = int(value)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("--seeds expects a positive integer, got %r" % value)
    if n < 1:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("--seeds expects a positive integer, got %r" % value)
    return n


def has_marker(text):
    return any(l.startswith("CONTROL ") or l.startswith("# Control") for l in text.split("\n"))


def names_counter(text, counter_shas):
    if not counter_shas:
        return True
    first = text.split("\n", 1)[0].lower()
    return any(s in first for s in counter_shas)


def selected(rel, globs):
    """True when a controls-relative path matches the globs as given or by basename."""
    rel = rel.lower()
    base = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(rel, p.lower()) or fnmatch.fnmatchcase(base, p.lower())
               for p in globs)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--round", type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--data-registry", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default=os.getcwd())
    ap.add_argument("--tip", default="HEAD")
    ap.add_argument("--shapes", default=DEFAULT_SHAPES)
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=seeds_arg, default=1, metavar="N",
                    help="distinct receipts required per named shape (default 1)")
    ap.add_argument("--receipt-glob", action="append", default=[], metavar="PATTERN",
                    help="controls-relative path or basename glob; repeatable "
                         "(default %s)" % ", ".join(DEFAULT_GLOBS))
    ap.add_argument("--any-md", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--counter-sha", action="append", type=sha_arg, default=[], metavar="SHA")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cdir = ".ufo/waves/round-%d/controls/" % a.round
    globs = a.receipt_glob or list(DEFAULT_GLOBS)
    rc, tip = git(a.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", a.tip + "^{commit}")
    if rc:
        print("UNEVALUABLE bad tip %s" % a.tip)
        return 2
    tip = tip.decode().strip()
    rc, files = git(a.repo, "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", tip, "--", cdir)
    if rc:
        print("UNEVALUABLE ls-tree failed")
        return 2
    receipts = []
    excluded_sha = 0
    excluded_glob = 0
    for f in files.decode().split("\n"):
        if not f:
            continue
        rel = f[len(cdir):] if f.startswith(cdir) else f
        if not selected(rel, globs):
            excluded_glob += 1
            continue
        rc, b = git(a.repo, "show", "%s:%s" % (tip, f))
        if rc:
            continue
        text = b.decode("utf-8", "replace")
        if f.lower().endswith(".md") and not (a.any_md or has_marker(text)):
            continue
        if not names_counter(text, a.counter_sha):
            excluded_sha += 1
            continue
        receipts.append(f)
    print("tip=%s round=%d receipts=%d counter_sha=%s excluded_by_counter_sha=%d "
          "receipt_glob=%s excluded_by_glob=%d seeds=%d"
          % (tip, a.round, len(receipts), ",".join(a.counter_sha) or "-", excluded_sha,
             ",".join(globs), excluded_glob, a.seeds))
    if not receipts:
        print("CONTROL_RECEIPTS verdict=FAIL reason=no-receipt-under-%s" % cdir)
        return 1
    rc, log = git(a.repo, "log", "--reverse", "--diff-filter=A", "--format=@%H %ct", "--name-only",
                  tip, "--", *receipts)
    if rc:
        print("UNEVALUABLE git log failed")
        return 2
    first = None
    cur = None
    for line in log.decode().split("\n"):
        if line.startswith("@"):
            h, ct = line[1:].split()
            cur = (h, int(ct))
        elif line.strip() and cur and first is None:
            first = cur
    if first is None:
        print("UNEVALUABLE no adding commit found")
        return 2
    rc, reg = git(a.repo, "show", "%s:%s" % (tip, a.data_registry))
    if rc:
        print("UNEVALUABLE data registry %s absent at tip" % a.data_registry)
        return 2
    try:
        created = json.loads(reg)["createdAt"]
        cts = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(created.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
    except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
        print("UNEVALUABLE createdAt unreadable: %r" % ex)
        return 2
    rt = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(first[1], datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
    print("receipt_commit=%s committed=%s data_registry=%s createdAt=%s"
          % (first[0][:12], rt, a.data_registry, created))
    order_ok = first[1] < cts
    names = [os.path.basename(r).lower() for r in receipts]
    counts = {}
    missing = []
    for shape in a.shapes.split(","):
        opts = [o.strip().lower() for o in shape.split("|") if o.strip()]
        n = sum(1 for name in names if any(o in name for o in opts))
        counts[shape] = n
        if n == 0:
            missing.append(shape)
    short = [s for s in counts if counts[s] < a.seeds]
    print("order=%s gap_s=%.0f shapes_missing=%s seeds_short=%s"
          % ("ok" if order_ok else "LATE", cts - first[1],
             ",".join(missing) or "-",
             ",".join("%s(%d<%d)" % (s, counts[s], a.seeds) for s in short) or "-"))
    print("shape_counts=%s" % ",".join("%s:%d" % (s, counts[s]) for s in counts))
    ok = order_ok and not missing and not short
    print("CONTROL_RECEIPTS verdict=%s" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL"))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Declarations are read from two grammars, and nothing else in the prose is in scope (free-text path-like tokens are references, proposals or upstream names, not declarations): Report: the trailer every seat dispatch requires under a `## Deliverables` heading, one `- \\`\\`` or `- ` bullet per deliverable (or `## Files written`, `Written:`) Resolution order for a declared path: as written if it contains `/`, else `/` where `` is `--seat-dir` or the report path with `.md` stripped (the lane's `w1/.md` + `w1//` convention). Modes: --repo R --rev REV --report P... prove each declaration with `git cat-file -e REV:path` --file P... A declaration is not found until one candidate exists.""" if path.startswith("/") or path.startswith("~") or "://" in path: return [] out = [] if not path.startswith(seat + "/"): out.append(f"{seat}/{path}") if path not in out: out.append(path) return out def main(argv=None): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--repo") ap.add_argument("--rev") ap.add_argument("--report", action="append", nargs="+", default=[]) ap.add_argument("--file", action="append", nargs="+", default=[]) ap.add_argument("--seat-dir") ap.add_argument("--require-declaration", action="store_true", help="fail a report that declares nothing (use over a wave dir at/after this criterion's round)") a = ap.parse_args(argv) a.report = [x for g in a.report for x in g] a.file = [x for g in a.file for x in g] reports = declared = exists = absent = undeclared = 0 def seat_for(path): if a.seat_dir: return a.seat_dir.rstrip("/") return path[:-3] if path.endswith(".md") else path if a.report: if not (a.repo and a.rev): print("CHECK101: --report needs --repo and --rev", file=sys.stderr) return 2 for path in a.report: blob = subprocess.run(("git", "-C", a.repo, "show", f"{a.rev}:{path}"), capture_output=True, text=True) if blob.returncode != 0: print(f"REPORT_UNRESOLVED rev={a.rev} report={path}") absent += 1 continue
